focus.title: 美国升级对华芯片出口管制，欧盟跟进审查成熟制程，全球供应链加速重构
focus.summary: 本周，美国商务部工业与安全局（BIS）发布新规，进一步扩大对华先进制程芯片及制造设备的出口管制范围，将更多中国芯片设计企业列入实体清单，并收紧对14nm及以下制程所需EDA软件、沉积设备的许可审查。欧盟委员会紧随其后，宣布将对华成熟制程芯片（28nm及以上）的依赖程度启动全面审查，评估其对欧洲汽车、工业设备等关键行业的影响。此外，日本经济产业省表示正考虑协同美国，对半导体相关物项实施更严格的对华出口限制。分析认为，此举标志着西方对华科技脱钩从先进制程向成熟制程延伸，全球半导体供应链正从全球化分工转向区域化、阵营化重构，中国出海企业面临设备采购、技术授权及客户尽调的多重合规挑战。
focus.source: 来源：美国商务部BIS公告、欧盟委员会声明、日本经济产业省表态 · 本周
focus.title_en: US Expands Chip Export Controls on China, EU Reviews Mature-Node Dependence, Global Supply Chains Reshape
focus.summary_en: This week, the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) issued new rules further expanding export controls on advanced chips and manufacturing equipment to China, adding more Chinese chip design firms to the Entity List and tightening license reviews for EDA software and deposition equipment for sub-14nm processes. The European Commission followed with an announcement of a comprehensive review of the EU's dependence on Chinese mature-node chips (28nm and above), assessing impacts on critical sectors like automotive and industrial equipment. Japan's METI also signaled potential coordination with the U.S. to impose stricter controls. Analysts view this as a shift from advanced-node to mature-node decoupling, accelerating the restructuring of global semiconductor supply chains from globalized division of labor to regional and bloc-based systems. Chinese companies going global face multifaceted compliance challenges in equipment procurement, technology licensing, and customer due diligence.
focus.source_en: Source: U.S. BIS announcement, European Commission statement, METI remarks · this week

case.title: 新加坡国际仲裁中心裁决：跨境并购中卖方隐瞒重大合规风险，买方获赔2.3亿美元
case.summary: 本周，新加坡国际仲裁中心（SIAC）公布一项裁决，涉及一起中国某上市公司收购东南亚某矿业公司的跨境并购纠纷。仲裁庭认定，卖方在交易文件中未披露其子公司长期违反当地环保法规、面临巨额罚款及吊销采矿许可的重大风险，构成欺诈性隐瞒，违反股权购买协议中的陈述与保证条款。仲裁庭裁定卖方需向买方支付2.3亿美元赔偿，包括交易对价差额、环境修复成本及律师费。该案凸显了跨境并购中，买方对目标公司合规状况的尽职调查深度不足，以及交易文件中对‘重大不利变化’和‘合规保证’条款的模糊表述可能带来的风险。对中国出海企业而言，此案警示：在投资‘一带一路’沿线国家时，应特别关注环境、劳工、反腐败等合规事项，并强化交易文件中的赔偿机制。
case.source: 来源：新加坡国际仲裁中心（SIAC）裁决摘要 · 本周
case.title_en: SIAC Award: Seller Concealed Major Compliance Risks in Cross-Border M&A, Buyer Awarded US$230 Million
case.summary_en: This week, the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) published an award concerning a cross-border M&A dispute where a Chinese listed company acquired a mining company in Southeast Asia. The tribunal found that the seller fraudulently concealed material non-compliance with local environmental regulations, including substantial fines and risk of license revocation, breaching representations and warranties in the share purchase agreement. The seller was ordered to pay US$230 million in damages, covering price adjustment, remediation costs, and legal fees. The case underscores the risks of insufficient compliance due diligence by buyers in cross-border deals and ambiguous 'MAE' and compliance warranty clauses. For Chinese companies going global, it highlights the need to focus on environmental, labor, and anti-corruption compliance in Belt and Road investments and to strengthen indemnity mechanisms in transaction documents.
case.source_en: Source: SIAC award summary · this week

policy.title: 粤港澳大湾区跨境数据流动新规落地，自贸区试点放宽‘数据出境’负面清单
policy.summary: 本周，国家网信办联合广东省政府发布《粤港澳大湾区（内地、香港、澳门）个人信息跨境流动标准合同办法》，在前期试点基础上，进一步扩大适用范围，明确符合条件的个人信息处理者可通过签订标准合同实现数据跨境流动，无需单独通过安全评估。同时，深圳前海、广州南沙、珠海横琴三个自贸片区推出‘数据出境负面清单’试点，对跨境贸易、跨境电商、国际物流等领域的数据出境，在负面清单之外的数据可自由流动。此举被视为中国在保障数据安全前提下，探索数据有序跨境流动的重要突破，为在大湾区运营的跨境企业提供了更明确、低成本的数据合规路径。企业需关注标准合同的备案要求、个人信息保护影响评估义务，以及负面清单的动态调整。
policy.source: 来源：国家网信办、广东省政府联合发布 · 本周
policy.title_en: New Cross-Border Data Flow Rules in Greater Bay Area: Pilot Negative Lists for Data Exports in FTZs
policy.summary_en: This week, the Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) and the Guangdong Provincial Government jointly issued the 'Standard Contract Measures for Cross-Border Flow of Personal Information in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (Mainland, Hong Kong, Macao)', expanding the scope of the earlier pilot. Eligible personal information processors can now transfer data cross-border by signing standard contracts, without separate security assessments. Simultaneously, the three free trade zones of Qianhai (Shenzhen), Nansha (Guangzhou), and Hengqin (Zhuhai) launched pilot 'negative lists' for data exports, allowing free flow of data outside the list in areas like cross-border trade, e-commerce, and international logistics. This marks a significant step in China's exploration of orderly cross-border data flow while safeguarding security, offering clearer and lower-cost compliance pathways for cross-border enterprises in the GBA. Companies should monitor filing requirements, personal information protection impact assessments, and dynamic adjustments to the negative lists.
policy.source_en: Source: Joint issuance by CAC and Guangdong Provincial Government · this week

analysis.title: 秦林蒿律师周度研判：地缘政治风险常态化，出海企业需构建‘合规韧性’与供应链备份
analysis.summary: 秦林蒿律师周度研判：本周美国对华芯片管制升级、欧盟启动成熟制程审查，叠加GBA跨境数据新规，显示国际经贸规则正从‘效率优先’转向‘安全优先’，地缘政治风险成为出海企业须常设考量的变量。建议企业：一、重新评估供应链地理布局，对关键元器件、软件、数据存储建立‘双备份’或‘多区域’方案，避免单一依赖；二、针对出口管制与制裁，建立内部筛查机制，对交易对手、最终用户、产品技术参数进行逐单合规审查；三、善用GBA数据跨境新规，通过标准合同与负面清单降低合规成本，但需完善个人信息保护影响评估；四、在跨境并购中，将目标公司合规尽调（尤其环境、制裁、数据）提升至与财务、法律同等权重，并在交易文件中细化赔偿条款。下周关注：美国国会可能推进的《2026年对外投资审查法案》对中资赴美投资的影响，以及欧盟对华电动车反补贴调查的终裁动向。
analysis.source: 来源：律连全球国际法律部 · 本周
analysis.title_en: Attorney Qin's Weekly View: Navigating Geopolitical Risks – Building Compliance Resilience and Supply Chain Redundancy
analysis.summary_en: Attorney Qin's weekly view: The escalation of U.S. chip controls and the EU's review of mature-node dependence, coupled with new GBA cross-border data rules, signal a shift in international trade rules from efficiency-first to security-first, making geopolitical risk a permanent consideration for going-global companies. Recommendations: 1) Reassess supply chain geography, establish dual or multi-region backups for critical components, software, and data storage to avoid single-point dependencies; 2) Implement internal screening mechanisms for export controls and sanctions, conducting transaction-specific compliance reviews of counterparties, end-users, and technical parameters; 3) Leverage GBA data transfer rules via standard contracts and negative lists to reduce compliance costs, while strengthening personal information protection impact assessments; 4) In cross-border M&A, elevate compliance due diligence (especially environmental, sanctions, and data) to the same weight as financial and legal, and detail indemnification clauses in transaction documents. Next week, watch for the U.S. Congress's potential advancement of the 'Outbound Investment Review Act of 2026' affecting Chinese investments, and the final ruling in the EU's anti-subsidy investigation into Chinese EVs.
analysis.source_en: Source: iGlobal Law International Legal Department · this week
